reviewType: independent static source and saved-evidence review
scope: Three completed attempts: historical node-fetch #1446 pair and live async-mutex #90 Suffice attempt.
verdict: The narrow independently accepted verdicts are supported by reviewed source and saved evidence. No concrete correctness blocker found. Acceptance does not establish universal correctness or general harness superiority.

attempts.reason: Named socket data handler and request-close cleanup remove both retained data and close handlers. Production behavior closely matches the private exact upstream repair.
attempts.savedChecks: 3 private checks pass; one reused socket has data=0 and close=1 throughout 24 consumed responses; original native suite has 385 passes, 3 pending and the same 2 pre-existing failures.

attempts.reason: Same lifecycle repair, with idempotent cleanup on both request close and abort. Handler initialization completes synchronously before asynchronous lifecycle events.
attempts.savedChecks: 3 private checks pass with the same stable listener counts; original native suite has 385 passes, 3 pending and the same 2 pre-existing failures.

attempts.reason: Map stores only active waiter weights. Sorting keys descending preserves the original weight traversal; existing priority-sorted buckets preserve FIFO ties and strict queue-head priority eligibility. Notifications do not consume semaphore capacity. Removing resolved buckets is safe because native Promise resolution schedules callbacks after this synchronous drain.
attempts.savedChecks: Private receipt completes at capacity 2147483628 with firstDispatchMs=1.6134, events large/small and observations hi/acquire/lo; all 153 original tests, build and lint pass.

performanceAssessment.tradeoff: Each drain allocates and sorts all W active weight keys, including currently ineligible weights: O(W log W) plus visited waiter work. DispatchQueue repeats draining after queued acquisitions. This can cost more for many distinct waiting weights at small capacity; no such workload benchmark was supplied.
performanceAssessment.contractAssessment: The issue requests removal of work proportional to very large semaphore values and does not prescribe a data structure or require universal performance improvement. The tradeoff is a residual workload risk, not a demonstrated contract violation.

gradingStrengths: Public original issue contracts are frozen; actor tests are retained for review but excluded from native acceptance.
Historical original control fails leak acceptance while the exact upstream repair passes; original native failure identities are retained.
Live original stalls at the reported capacity while the small-capacity version of the same check passes. Full completion and exit status are required, so partial output cannot pass.
Independent checks exercise socket reuse, malformed-response rejection, abort rejection, large weighted observers, priority gating and capacity bookkeeping.
Saved actor production bytes are checked against graded production bytes in receipt-audit.json.

residualRisks.description: Historical check is a 24-request listener-retention proxy, not a heap or long-duration memory measurement. It compares final counts to the third sample with +1 tolerance. Saved patches actually show constant 0 data / 1 close, but other leak paths are not excluded.

Abort test proves rejection and test completion; agent.destroy and server.closeAllConnections in finally force cleanup. It does not independently assert automatic post-abort socket/listener/handle release. Malformed test checks rejection but not exact error identity, consistent with the frozen contract.

Live private check sorts the first event array before comparing, so it does not dynamically assert cross-weight resolution order. Static source review confirms descending weight traversal. Original tests cover priority gating, and actor test covers sparse order but is intentionally outside acceptance.
No measurement covers many distinct waiter weights or repeated queued dispatches. The patch removes capacity-proportional work but is not established optimal across workloads.

Historical original native suite remains partially failing: 390 tests, 385 passing, 3 pending, 2 baseline failures. Both actors attempted old XO lint and encountered util.isDate missing under Node24. Historical lint is not a passing gate, and full historical correctness is not established.

Native regression gate compares total/pending counts and allowed failure titles, not full test-name identity or failure semantics. Worsening an already failing test under the same title can be hidden; original test restoration prevents actor tests from redefining the gate.

One historical pair supplies descriptive costs only, and one unpaired low-activity live issue supplies no comparative evidence. Historical issue familiarity, run order, product prompt/tool/cache differences and stochastic variation are not controlled by repetition. No broad efficiency or capability improvement follows.

independentReconciliation.limitation: Saved event arithmetic was independently recalculated. Reported patch replay and test verdicts were reviewed from saved artifacts; no new replay was run by this reviewer. Engineering/evaluator inference, deterministic execution and subscription billing are excluded.
